actionResult.summary: Review 216 Proposal：OpenSpec resolved executable authority、real OpenSpec Full Test fail-closed、A1 stable point-in-time fixture、Verification self-closure、performance/no-scheduler 与 16-selector implementation surface 均承接 214/215 approved Explore；但 checkpoint hygiene contract 超出了 approved Proof 5。214 Proof 5 只对 real OpenSpec archive 实际复现的 redundant EOF blank lines / exactly one final newline 给出 PASS，并明确没有证据支持更宽 formatting authority；216 Proposal/Design/spec/tasks 却新增了 touched text files 的 trailing spaces/tabs removal。Proposal 只能冻结 Explore 已证明的 boundary，不能把未证明的 whitespace class 扩成 Executor authority。应 revise-propose 将 checkpoint normalization 收回 EOF-only proof-backed scope；如坚持 trailing spaces/tabs，则需先通过合法 Explore generation 补相应 external-mutation/authority proof。

reviewFindings.title: Checkpoint hygiene authority exceeds the approved EOF-only Explore proof
reviewFindings.problem: 214/215 approved Explore Proof 5 proves only a bounded EOF normalization after real OpenSpec 1.7 archive: collapse redundant EOF blank lines and preserve exactly one final newline. The Explore in-scope boundary likewise says EOF-only terminal whitespace normalization, and its Evidence/Gap explicitly says no evidence supports broad formatting authority. 216 Proposal, Design Decision 6, flowkit-archive-and-checkpoint-boundary spec, and task 4.2 expand the same Owner checkpoint authorization to also remove trailing spaces/tabs from touched text files. That additional transformation class was not established by the approved Explore evidence.
reviewFindings.contractRef: Flowkit Explore Skill v2 §4.7 External Mutation Proof / §5 Proof Acceptance Depth / approved 214 Explore Proof 5
reviewFindings.invariant: Proposal may freeze only implementation/authority boundaries whose acceptance boundary is covered by approved Explore evidence; a proof-backed EOF-only mechanical normalization must not be silently widened into a larger Executor mutation authority.
evidence: 214 explore.md Scope Boundary: in scope is explicitly EOF-only terminal whitespace normalization — redundant EOF blank lines / exactly one final newline.
214 explore.md Proof 5 Acceptance Boundary permits only collapsing redundant EOF blank lines and preserving exactly one final newline.
214 explore.md Proof 5 Gap states: None for the bounded EOF rule. No evidence supports broad formatting authority.
216 proposal.md adds trailing spaces/tabs cleanup to checkpoint mechanics.
216 design.md Decision 6 allows remove trailing spaces/tabs for touched text files under the same authorize-checkpoint fact.
216 flowkit-archive-and-checkpoint-boundary spec and task 4.2 freeze the same unproved trailing-space/tab authority.
reviewFindings.impact: If approved as written, I1 would give the Executor a broader post-archive file-mutation authority than the approved Explore actually proved. That weakens the detached exact-candidate / mechanical-checkpoint boundary and turns a proof-backed EOF correction into an unproven generalized whitespace normalization rule.
reviewFindings.requiredOutcome: Revise the Proposal generation so checkpoint normalization is limited to the approved EOF-only rule: collapse redundant EOF blank lines and ensure exactly one final newline on candidate/archive-touched text files, with semantic/internal formatting/unrelated-file changes fail-closed. Do not include trailing spaces/tabs removal unless that broader class is first supported by a new legitimate Explore proof/authority boundary.
acceptance: Proposal/Design/spec/tasks no longer authorize generic trailing spaces/tabs removal under the existing checkpoint authorization.
Allowed checkpoint normalization matches approved Proof 5 exactly: redundant EOF blank-line collapse plus exactly one final newline, limited to candidate/archive-touched text files.
Forbidden scope continues to include Markdown reflow, internal/semantic formatting changes, unrelated files, and broad formatter execution.
git diff --check and staged git diff --cached --check remain required after normalization.
The 16-selector apply/revise-apply surface remains otherwise unchanged unless a separately justified Proposal correction requires a different already-proven path.
